head.i: De Phr. si, Homines possunt cre-dere, si velint.

main_text.p: QVIA hæc phrasis, Homines pos-sunt credere, si velint, quæ in scriptis AMYRALDI nonnunquam occurrit, secus intellecta, nonnemini videtur vel absurda, quasi velle credere esset credere ipsum, vel periculosa, quasi hominum arbitrio libero in rebus ad salutem pertinentibus quidquam tri-bueret, est hic etiam paucis verbis ex-plicanda.

Quum fides ex duobus rebus existat, objecto quod ad credendum proponitur, & mentis ad objectum amplectendum operatione atque appulsu, homines dicuntur posse credere si velint vel respectu objecti, vel respectu mentis & facultatis quæ se se ad objectum ap-plicat.
Et objectum quidem duplici ratione proponitur, distinctè scilicet, & con-fusius. Quibus autem offertur τὸ πλέον[?] confusius, illi sanè distinctè credere

page.notes: Page number "42" is read from a small superscript-style figure; the Greek word after "offertur" is hard to make out and is marked [?]. Long s has been normalised to s throughout (printed as s or f in the scan). Printed hyphens at line ends are kept as "cre-dere", "pos-sunt", "tri-bueret", "ex-plicanda", "ap-plicat" and "con-fusius". The paragraph ends mid-sentence and continues on the next page.
